newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bonds extend the uptrend after ECI.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds extend the uptrend after ECI.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures appear destined to drift sideways to higher while waiting for more key fundamental data to hit late week, analysts said Tuesday.
September bonds edged past last week's 1-1/2-year peak of 115-23/32 early, popping up on news of modest growth in U.S. labor costs, and resumed their climb in the afternoon.
The 0.8-percent rise in the second-quarter employment cost index was in line with market expectations.
Bond futures remain outrageously overbought and in need of a correction but can find little followthrough on dips, analysts acknowledged.
"It looks like for now we're just content to look higher," said Cia Lallas, technical analyst for MMS International Inc.
Supporting the case for still more gains is the contract's ability to trade consistently in the upper half of the trend channel ever since touching bottom on June 30, Lallas said.
The top of the channel currently lies at 116-05, she said. Below the market, there is strong support at the July 11 high of 113-15/32.
Before a clearer picture of U.S. economic growth emerges Thursday and Friday, prices are unlikely to break out of the channel, Lallas said.
Advance second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product data will be released Thursday, followed on Friday by July employment statistics.

To some chart watchers, though, it is just a matter of time before bonds retrench. "I think the market's entitled to a rest," said Michael Krauss, chief technical strategist for Chase Securities Inc, noting that bond futures have risen 10 full points from the April low of 105-30/32.
Krauss warned it would be very tough for September futures to surpass resistance at 116-28/32 and predicted the rally would stall in the mid-116-00s.

Recent commitments of traders data showing commercial hedgers are heavily short the market and indications that commodities prices have bottomed are two of the warning flags he is heeding, Krauss said.
A close below Monday's low of 114-28/32 is needed to confirm a market top, he said.
